canonical_topic: Topping Cycle vs. Bottoming Cycle Cogeneration
definition: Topping cycle cogeneration uses waste heat from the condenser (produced after generating power) for an external purpose; bottoming cycle cogeneration instead uses heat from an external industrial process to supply or reduce the plant's own boiler fuel needs.
core_idea: The two terms distinguish the direction of the heat exchange: topping cycle exports the plant's waste heat outward, while bottoming cycle imports outside process heat inward to cut the plant's own fuel use.
key_points: Topping cycle: condenser waste heat is reused externally after power generation
Bottoming cycle: heat from an external industrial process feeds the plant's boiler, reducing or eliminating its fuel needs
